subproblem.title: A left one-coboundary cups to a level two-boundary
subproblem.statement: Let k be a field, G a group, Ω=AlgebraicClosure ℚ, r:G→Autℚ(Ω) a group homomorphism, and A,B,N k-representations of G. Let φ:A→ₗ[k]B→ₗ[k]N be equivariant: φ(s·a,s·b)=s·φ(a,b) for all s,a,b. Fix a∈A and a one-cocycle g:G→B satisfying g(st)=s·g(t)+g(s). Assume g is level, meaning that some finite-dimensional rational intermediate field F⊆Ω satisfies g(th)=g(t) whenever r(h) fixes F. Define d₀a(s)=s·a−a. Then cupCochain φ (d₀a) g belongs to levelCoboundaries₂ r N, the image of the level one-cochains under d₁v(s,t)=s·v(t)−v(st)+v(s).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {k G : Type} [Field k] [Group G] (r : G →* (AlgebraicClosure ℚ ≃ₐ[ℚ] AlgebraicClosure ℚ)) (A B N : Rep.{0} k G) (φ : A →ₗ[k] B →ₗ[k] N), (∀ (s : G) (a : A) (b : B), φ (A.ρ s a) (B.ρ s b) = N.ρ s (φ a b)) → ∀ (a : A) (g : groupCohomology.cocycles₁ B), groupCohomology.IsLevelConstant₁ r (⇑g) → groupCohomology.cupCochain φ (fun s : G => A.ρ s a - a) (⇑g) ∈ groupCohomology.levelCoboundaries₂ r N
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix the stated data. Choose a finite-dimensional rational intermediate field F witnessing the level property of g, and define v:G→N by v(t)=φ(a,g(t)).
2. If r(h) fixes F, then v(th)=φ(a,g(th))=φ(a,g(t))=v(t). Thus the same F witnesses IsLevelConstant₁ r v, so v is a member of levelCochains₁ r N.
3. For arbitrary s,t∈G, equivariance gives s·φ(a,g(t))=φ(s·a,s·g(t)), and the one-cocycle identity gives g(st)=s·g(t)+g(s). Therefore d₁v(s,t)=φ(s·a,s·g(t))−φ(a,s·g(t)+g(s))+φ(a,g(s))=φ(s·a,s·g(t))−φ(a,s·g(t))=φ(s·a−a,s·g(t)), using linearity in the second argument to cancel φ(a,g(s)) and linearity in the first argument for the last equality.
4. The final expression is cupCochain φ (fun s↦s·a−a) g evaluated at (s,t). Equality at every pair gives equality of the two cochains. Since levelCoboundaries₂ r N is precisely the image of levelCochains₁ r N under (d₁₂ N).hom, the level cochain v is a preimage of the required cup cochain. This proves its membership in levelCoboundaries₂ r N.
proof_key_steps: Choose v(t)=φ(a,g(t)) as the boundary primitive.
Use the level field of g to prove that v is level.
Compute d₁v=cupCochain φ (d₀a) g using equivariance and the cocycle identity.
Use the defining image description of levelCoboundaries₂.

audit.reason: The standalone Lean proposition matches the prose and all its hypotheses. The primitive v(t)=φ(a,g(t)) inherits g's level field. Equivariance, the cocycle identity, and bilinearity give d₁v=cupCochain φ (d₀a) g with the correct sign. This supplies exactly the preimage required by levelCoboundaries₂. No additional action hypothesis or child dependency is needed; the proof is complete and non-circular.
